The question is objectionable because the defendant’s attorney did not lay a proper foundation for impeaching his own witness. A party may use a prior inconsistent statement against his own witness only after showing that the testimony is unexpected and affirmatively damaging, and after confronting the witness with the time, place, and circumstances of the earlier statement; calling the testimony a recent fabrication and referring only to “a grand jury” does not do that. Temporal proximity does not make the grand-jury statement admissible.

CONFIDENCE: 74
